Course 04

Personality without labels

Traits, differences and assessment.

Lesson 1. What personality is

1 · Lesson

Personality is the set of relatively stable ways of thinking, feeling and acting that distinguish one person from another. "Relatively" is the key word: we are recognisable over time, but not identical in every situation.

Many theories have been proposed over history: the humours of ancient medicine, Jung's typologies, psychoanalytic models, social learning theories and trait theories. The latter are the most used in research today because they allow measurement and comparison.

A trait is a dimension on which everyone scores somewhere, not a box. One is not "introverted" or "extraverted" the way one is left- or right-handed: most of us are in the middle ranges, and few people are at the extremes.

2 · Example

A person can be very talkative with friends and quiet in work meetings. That does not mean they "have no personality", but that personality is expressed in interaction with the situation. What is stable is the pattern: in which situations they tend to talk and in which they do not.

3 · Activity

Think of three very different situations in your week (work, family, leisure). Describe how you behave in each. What stays the same? What changes?
